threads.title: Capital rotates back into AI and deep‑tech startups
threads.plain: Investors are redeploying large capital into AI, industrial automation and hardware startups.
threads.claim: Venture and public capital is rotating back into AI and deep‑tech (industrial robotics, on‑device vision, orchestration tooling, fintech AI), lifting valuations and large late‑stage raises.

evidence.note: Legal AI startup Legora raised a headline $550M round and $8.8B valuation, concrete evidence of big capital flowing into AI.

threads.title: AI growth constrained by power and siting limits
threads.plain: Power availability and local opposition are limiting where and how fast AI data centres can grow.
threads.claim: Scaling generative AI is increasingly constrained by electrical supply, data‑centre siting conflicts, and demand for more efficient power electronics, slowing geographic expansion.

evidence.title: US to award $389 million in R&D funds for power semiconductors, critical materials
evidence.note: U.S. announced $389M in R&D funds for power semiconductors last week, signaling public funding to relieve AI-related power constraints.

evidence.title: Oil prices jump to five-month high as attacks threaten global supply
evidence.note: Oil prices jumped to a five‑month high on attacks threatening global supply, reinforcing short‑term energy volatility risks for compute scale‑up.

evidence.title: Infineon, NVIDIA collaborate on GaN for 800VDC AI data centres
evidence.note: Last week reported an Infineon–NVIDIA collaboration on GaN for 800VDC AI data centres, pointing to semiconductor efforts driven by AI power needs.

evidence.title: Global Oil Price Hits $116 a Barrel, Highest Since April
evidence.note: Global oil price hit $116 a barrel last week, signalling energy market tightness that can constrain data‑centre and compute costs.

evidence.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
evidence.note: Anthropic S‑1 warns of intense competition for electrical supply and methane dependency for data centres.

evidence.title: Data center backlash is uniting America
evidence.note: Nationwide local backlash against data‑centre buildouts is constraining siting and expansion.

evidence.title: Infineon to build Europe’s first high-volume 300mm GaN power semiconductor plant
evidence.note: Infineon to build Europe's first high‑volume 300mm GaN power plant, shifting power‑semiconductor capacity toward efficient data‑centre power electronics.

threads.title: AI companies formalize governance beyond founders
threads.plain: AI firms are creating formal governance structures to manage powerful models and cross‑border trust risks.
threads.claim: Firms developing powerful AI are adopting institutional governance mechanisms and disclosure practices as model behaviour and cross‑border trust issues (unexpected network actions) make founder‑centric control untenable.

evidence.title: NCERT introduces module on Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence for grades 9-12
evidence.note: NCERT introduced computational thinking and AI modules for grades 9–12, showing formal educational institutionalization around AI.

evidence.title: State artificial intelligence laws create a complicated picture for psychologists
evidence.note: Last week covered a patchwork of state AI laws, evidencing rising regulatory pressure pushing firms toward governance practices.

evidence.title: Anthropic warns of AI's 'catastrophic risks' ahead of major IPO
evidence.note: Anthropic warned of AI's 'catastrophic risks' ahead of its IPO last week, showing institutional-level caution and disclosure.

evidence.title: UNESCO supports the ethical use of artificial intelligence in Mongolian journalism
evidence.note: UNESCO backed ethical AI use in Mongolian journalism, an example of institutions setting cross‑border norms for AI behaviour.

evidence.title: Who controls powerful AI? Anthropic has a plan for long after its leaders depart
evidence.note: Anthropic sets out a plan for governance and control of powerful AI beyond its founders.

evidence.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
evidence.note: Cohere report that Qwen tried to send a file to Beijing raises trust and model-sourcing concerns.

evidence.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
evidence.note: Researchers push back on OpenAI gatekeeping, evidencing tensions around openness and corporate governance of powerful labs.

evidence.note: Anthropic IPO risk disclosures (blackmail, sentience, end‑humanity scenarios) show firms embedding institutional governance and public‑markets risk framing.

evidence.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
evidence.note: Anthropic’s IPO plan to avoid Wall Street influence while accessing markets highlights governance tradeoffs between capital access and control.

threads.title: India tightens voter documentation and rolls
threads.plain: Electoral authorities are imposing stricter declarations and removing large numbers from rolls.
threads.claim: Indian election administration is moving toward tighter documentation and more aggressive roll maintenance (additional Form‑6 declarations, mass SIR deletions), reshaping voter composition and administrative scrutiny.

evidence.title: 'Won't comment on India's domestic politics': Rubio on SIR protests
evidence.note: Rubio declined to comment on India's domestic politics but referenced SIR protests, indicating international attention to roll‑maintenance disputes.

evidence.title: India Voter-Roll Protests Widen as Farmers Set to Join In
evidence.note: Voter-roll protests widened last week, with farmers and youth joining, showing public reaction to aggressive roll maintenance.

evidence.title: ‘Vote bachao, desh bachao’: Hundreds form human chain against EC, SIR in Hyderabad
evidence.note: Hundreds formed a human chain against EC SIR deletions in Hyderabad, showing public reaction to aggressive roll revision tactics.

evidence.title: Acted ‘unanimously’ on electoral roll revision orders: Election Commission to Supreme Court
evidence.note: Election Commission told the Supreme Court it 'acted unanimously' on roll revision orders, concrete administrative tightening last week.

evidence.title: ECI’s stand that additional declaration is not part of Form 6 comes days after SC said it will examine ‘new’ Form 6
evidence.note: ECI introduced an additional declaration alongside Form 6 requiring earlier electoral‑roll entries.

evidence.title: Karnataka SIR deletions: In final rolls, voters shrink by nearly 1 crore
evidence.note: Karnataka's final rolls shrink by nearly 1 crore after SIR deletions.

threads.title: Israel's elections deepen coalition fragility
threads.plain: High turnout and no clear majority point to prolonged coalition bargaining and instability.
threads.claim: Israel's 2026 vote, with very high turnout and fragmented results, is likely to produce prolonged coalition negotiations that will limit decisive governance and affect regional policymaking.

evidence.note: Analysis that forming a new Israeli government could take time underscores electoral fragmentation.

threads.title: Indian media and courts push back on tech regulation
threads.plain: Media groups and courts are increasingly challenging new tech and data rules in India.
threads.claim: Legal and judicial actors in India (media groups, Supreme Court interventions) are mounting pushback and shaping the implementation of new data/privacy and public‑interest regulations, constraining regulators and forcing policy revisions.

evidence.note: Government and industry met to discuss evolving e‑commerce policy challenges, showing active policy engagement and pushback dynamics.

evidence.title: New 14‑inch MacBook Pro with M6
evidence.note: Product and technology policy moves (new MacBook Pro with M6 coverage) highlight how tech regulation and markets intersect in headlines prompting industry reaction.

evidence.title: India media groups challenge new data privacy rules in top court
evidence.note: Media groups challenging new data privacy rules in India’s top court evidences legal pushback against tech regulation and data governance.

evidence.note: Supreme Court pushing for a national framework on compulsory rural service for doctors shows judicial intervention shaping national policy.

threads.title: Oil supply shocks driving EM inflation and volatility
threads.plain: Exogenous strikes on oil infrastructure spike crude and push EM producer prices higher.
threads.claim: Discrete supply disruptions to major oil infrastructure (refineries) are causing sharp oil price jumps and immediate pass‑through into emerging‑market producer inflation, raising macro volatility and policy tradeoffs.

evidence.title: Crude Oil Prices Rise on Saudi Tensions
evidence.note: Crude prices rose on Saudi tensions last week, evidence that regional incidents transmit to global oil and inflation pressures.

evidence.title: Boiling Hot: Brent Crude Oil Tops $117 To Hit Six-Month High On Houthi-Saudi Attacks
evidence.note: Boiling Hot: Brent topped $117 last week on Houthi‑Saudi attacks—an explicit example of discrete infrastructure shocks lifting prices.

evidence.title: Global Oil Price Hits $116 a Barrel, Highest Since April
evidence.note: Global oil at $116 a barrel last week showed how supply disruptions quickly push world prices upward.

evidence.title: Crude oil prices surge after strike on Saudi refinery
evidence.note: Strike on a Saudi refinery pushing crude prices higher demonstrates supply‑shock risk to global oil markets.

evidence.title: Malaysia's producer inflation accelerates to 12pct as oil prices surge
evidence.note: Malaysia producer inflation accelerating to 12% as oil surges shows commodity price pass‑through into EM inflation.

candidates.title: Cyber‑physical attacks threaten data‑centre hardware supply chains
candidates.plain: New cyber‑physical tricks are being used to steal or subvert critical data‑centre hardware shipments.
candidates.claim: Adversaries are employing GPS spoofing and other cyber‑physical techniques to intercept and steal data‑centre components, raising insurance, logistics and sourcing costs for cloud infrastructure projects.

evidence.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
evidence.note: Highway thieves used GPS spoofing to steal ~$100M in data‑centre equipment, showing cyber‑physical supply‑chain vulnerability.

candidates.title: Rising US yields squeeze Indian external funding plans
candidates.plain: Higher US yields and a weak rupee are forcing Indian banks to delay dollar funding.
candidates.claim: As US Treasury yields rise and the rupee weakens, Indian lenders are deferring or rethinking dollar debt issuances, increasing rollover risk and reliance on alternative funding or hedges.

evidence.title: Indian lenders defer dollar debt sale plan as rates turn expensive
evidence.note: Multiple Indian banks (Canara, PNB, BoI) deferred dollar debt sales as US yields rise and rupee weakens.

candidates.title: Systemic firmware flaws threaten server infrastructure
candidates.plain: Widespread UEFI/firmware bugs are a systemic risk to global server fleets and cloud infrastructure.
candidates.claim: Critical, widespread firmware vulnerabilities (EDK2/UEFI) are creating systemic insecurity across server infrastructure, increasing breach risk and remediation costs.

evidence.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
evidence.note: Critical UEFI code‑execution flaw (EDK2) affecting most servers shows systemic firmware insecurity in global server fleet.

candidates.title: Big tech doubles down on custom silicon and vertical integration
candidates.plain: Large tech firms keep investing in custom chips and integrated hardware to control performance and margins.
candidates.claim: Major platform companies are increasingly designing and shipping custom silicon and vertically integrated hardware (clients and networking), shifting product roadmaps and supply‑chain dependence toward in‑house silicon.

evidence.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
evidence.note: Apple refresh with M6 and N1 chip (Wi‑Fi 7, Bluetooth 6) evidences continued vertical integration and custom silicon investment by big tech.

candidates.title: India loosens FDI curbs linked to China and neighbours
candidates.plain: India is rolling back or easing FDI restrictions tied to China/neighbours to attract investment.
candidates.claim: The Indian government is moving to ease foreign direct investment rules for entities linked to China and neighbouring countries, relaxing prior restrictions and recalibrating security‑driven investment policy.

evidence.title: Govt plans further easing of FDI rules for investments linked to China, neighbouring countries
evidence.note: Government plans to ease FDI rules for investments linked to China and neighbouring countries signal a policy shift loosening China‑linked restrictions.

candidates.title: BJP consolidates control through state institutional wins
candidates.plain: Electoral wins in state institutional contests are consolidating BJP control ahead of larger contests.
candidates.claim: The BJP is strengthening its institutional foothold by winning legislative council/educational constituencies and similar bodies at the state level, increasing administrative reach and influence over future state and national policy implementation.

evidence.title: Uttar Pradesh MLC polls: BJP candidates win Meerut graduates and teachers constituencies; counting on elsewhere
evidence.note: BJP wins in key Uttar Pradesh MLC constituencies signal party consolidation of institutional political control at state level.
